title: Maigret Username Search
description: Type a username and press Start. Maigret checks the 500 most popular sites in about a minute and lists every account it finds, with the name, bio, followers and other usernames on each profile. Empty the Number of sites field to check all 5,000+ sites.

usernames.title: Usernames to search (usernames)
usernames.description: Enter the usernames to search, one per line, for example soxoj. You can paste an @handle, several usernames separated by commas, or a profile link such as https://github.com/soxoj, and the username is read from it. Each username is searched on its own. Same as the USERNAMES argument of the maigret command.

maxSites.title: Number of sites (maxSites)
maxSites.description: Enter how many sites to check for each username, most popular first. Leave it empty to check all 5,000+ sites in Maigret's database, about 4 minutes per username on Apify; 500 covers the popular sites in about a minute. Same as --top-sites in the maigret command, and empty is the same as -a (all sites).

tags.title: Site types or countries (tags)
tags.description: Enter site types to check only those sites, such as social, forum, gaming, coding, dating, crypto, finance, music or shopping, or countries as names or two-letter codes (India, us, de). Sites with any of these tags are checked. Leave it empty to check every kind of site, adult and dating sites included. Same as --tags in the maigret command.

recursive.title: Follow linked names (recursive)
recursive.description: Choose whether to also search the other usernames Maigret finds on the profiles, such as a Twitter handle linked from a GitHub page. On by default, up to 3 linked usernames per run; their profiles are saved and billed like the ones you typed, and each row says where the username was found. Same as Maigret's recursive search (--no-recursion turns it off).

details.title: Read profile details (details)
details.description: Choose whether to read each found profile page for details: name, bio, location, follower count, join date, photo, links, account IDs and other usernames. On by default, and needed to follow linked names. Turning it off makes a scan a little faster. Same as Maigret's info extraction (--no-extracting turns it off).

timeout.title: Wait per site (timeout)
timeout.description: Enter how many seconds to wait for each site before giving up on it: 30 by default (Maigret's own default), from 5 to 120. Raise it for more complete results from slow sites; lower it for a faster scan. Same as --timeout in the maigret command.

retries.title: Retries per site (retries)
retries.description: Enter how many more times to check a site that did not answer: 0 by default (Maigret's own default), up to 3. Each retry re-checks only the sites that failed, so it adds time but finds accounts on busy sites. Same as --retries in the maigret command.
